title: Continuous coefficient matrices and pointwise integral cosets
statement: For the coefficient sheaves A_X and K_X on X_proet [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], define the section-matrix lattice image of G ∈ GL_n(C(|V|,K)) by integral linear combinations of its columns. Right multiplication by a continuous integral invertible matrix preserves the image. If every pointwise coset of G equals the coset of a fixed h ∈ GL_n(K), its image equals the constant-matrix lattice image of h.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; Continuous coefficient matrices and pointwise integral cosets

proof.text: Lift the entries of a continuous coefficient matrix and its inverse to A-valued continuous functions whenever both are pointwise integral. The subtype topology gives continuity and injectivity of coefficient inclusion gives the inverse equations.

proof.text: Prove invariance under integral right multiplication by reindexing the finite column sum; use the inverse matrix for the opposite inclusion. Lift h⁻¹G by the first step and apply invariance; the constant-matrix formula is definitional.
